Your question implies much more than is apparent on the surface, and their is no ultimate, authoritative, "correct" answer. For me, this question is the exact reason for the Bible's existence. The journey of questioning, analysing, and introspection. It comprises historical events, which can sometimes be accurately researched (but not always), lineages also, may give an air of factuality and creedence, but the message of the moral teachings, allegories, instruction, advice, and parables are only valuable to oneself when they result in a person's own thinking and actions.

To take a scientific discipline to try to prove a belief only serves to enhance its validity, but does not prove it. Humans interpret reality by repeatable tests with the same outcomes, but are still known as theories. Increased instances will add to the perceived truth, but that implies there will never be a future incident which disagrees with that expected outcome and until time ceases it remains a possibility however slight.

To me, the bottom line is faith. Hebrews 11 talks about what faith is - "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen" - and gives examples of what faith has accomplished in the lives of Bible era persons. It is by faith that I read the Bible and by faith assume Divine guidance and inspiration to have my interpretation result in my living a life that is of benefit to myself, my family, and community. Faith also gives me reason to persevere when I don't have evidence of its fruition yet, or ever.

The old adage of "life's a journey, not a destination" helps me to realise I will never reach a finish line or end to my understanding of my purpose. I find the Bible, and all my questions associated with it, a life-long discovery process and wish you well on yours.
